title: Kayak Analyzer Solver Run
description: One Kayak Analyzer solver run. FRAME: every position in this document is in the HULL's own frame — the uploaded STL after auto-orientation to Z-up, with X = LOA (bow at +X), Y = beam, Z up — in millimetres, and every height is measured from the keel, the hull's lowest Z. Angles follow the solver's conventions: trim + is bow up, heel + drops the -Y side.

model_hash.description: SHA256 of the STL model used, as 64 lowercase hex characters — the mesh's identity everywhere (roster key, re-pick check). Hashed over the raw bytes, never the parsed geometry, so the x1000 metre-Apply rescale keeps one identity.

weight_kg.description: Paddler plus gear plus boat, kg. The bounds are the app's own form gate: under 20 kg is not a loaded boat, over 200 kg is not a load this hull class is solved for.

lcg_pct_lwl.description: LCG as % of LWL from bow

kg_mm.description: Vertical center of gravity above keel in mm — a HEIGHT, never an absolute Z. Required: the UI exposes KG, and a run that does not state its KG cannot be reproduced. The solver's fallback when a caller omits it is 280 mm (DEFAULT_KG_MM). Above 1000 mm the CG sits above the deck of any kayak, where GM stops describing anything real.

heel_deg.description: Fixed heel in degrees; + heels the -Y side down. Required: GM and the whole GZ curve depend on it, so a run that does not state its heel cannot be reproduced. The solver's default when a caller omits it is 0 (upright). The app's slider spans ±30.

draft_mm.description: Equilibrium draft at midship, mm, measured up from the keel

trim_deg.description: Trim in degrees; + is bow up (marine convention)

lwl_mm.description: Length of waterline in mm, measured at the waterline (not the bounding box)

bwl_mm.description: Beam at waterline in mm, measured at the waterline

volume_liters.description: Displaced volume in liters; fresh water, so 1 L = 1 kg = 1_000_000 mm3

lcb_xyz.description: LCB in mm [x, y, z], in the hull's own frame

lcg_xyz.description: LCG in mm [x, y, z], in the hull's own frame

lcb_lcg_offset_mm.description: The longitudinal LCB-LCG offset the SOLVER reports, in mm: the distance between the two centres measured in the POSED frame — the frame the waterplane is horizontal in, which is the frame trim equilibrium is a property of. It is the residual the trim sweep closes on, and it is NOT |lcb_xyz[0] - lcg_xyz[0]|: the hull pitches about pivot_xyz, and that difference carries the pivot term the pose removes (on the test hull at 75 kg the two differ about 6x). Carried by the format, never re-derived by a reader.

pivot_xyz.description: The rotation centre the solve pitched the hull about, mm [x, y, z], hull frame. Its x is the LCG's x but its z is the bounding-box centre's z — NOT the LCG (a KG height), so it must be carried rather than guessed.

bow_freeboard_mm.description: Bow stem tip above the waterline, mm, in the hull's own frame

stern_freeboard_mm.description: Stern stem tip above the waterline, mm, in the hull's own frame

waterline_z_mm.description: Waterline plane height at midship, mm, in the hull's own frame; draft_mm is this minus the keel

min_freeboard_mm.description: Optional: the stem-tip clearance at this heel (the smaller of the bow and stern freeboards), mm. Carried by the app's export; the reader recomputes the end-tip immersion angle from it.

gz_curve.description: Optional: the righting-arm curve, one sample per heel angle. Emitted by the app's export; absent on a trimmed record.

waterline_polygon.description: Waterline polygon points [x, y] in mm. NOT currently emitted: clipBelowPlane walks the contour to get its area and second moment, then discards the points. Returning them means changing the clipper's return type.

lcf_mm.description: Longitudinal centre of flotation in mm: an ABSOLUTE x in the hull's own frame, the same datum as lcb_xyz[0] and lcg_xyz[0] — not a distance from midship

tpc.description: Tonnes per centimetre immersion at the waterline

phase.description: How far the run went. This app imports full_coefficients only: a draft_only or trim_lcg_lcb run has no coefficients block, and the reader requires one.

file_name.description: Optional: the source STL's file name, for display
